title: Automatic Synthesis of Specialized Hash Functions
problem: General-purpose hash functions provide suboptimal performance for keys with known patterns (fixed-length, common subsequences, or predetermined byte sequences). Achieving 2-11% speedup over STL and Abseil libraries requires specialized hash function generation.
motivation: Hash table performance is critical in many applications; specialized hashing reduces hash computation bottleneck when key structure is predictable.
method: Uses code generation with regex pattern identification and synthesis from key examples. Two algorithms: one identifies relevant regex patterns within key distributions, the other generates optimized hash functions based on identified expressions. Outperforms general-purpose hashes by exploiting key format regularity.
key_novelty: Automated synthesis of format-specific hash functions via regex pattern learning from key examples rather than hand-tuned templates.
contributions: Technique for synthesizing hash functions specialized to byte format patterns
Algorithms for regex extraction and code generation from key examples
Speedups of 2-11% on full benchmarks, up to 50x on hashing-only microbenchmarks
limitations: Limited to keys with discoverable patterns; performance gains depend on key distribution regularity.
primary_theme: specialized code generation for hash functions
